title: Round 5 / ECDLP-14: well-posed intermediate targets with attached lower bounds
question: Formulate precise intermediate targets between the known Theta(sqrt r) generic bound and the O(n log n) universal target (exact models: generic/black-box group ops, algebraic straight-line programs over F_q, multitape TM bit complexity; worst-case vs average; with/without preprocessing; restricted families), and for each state the best known lower and upper bounds with verified sources, identifying which targets are (a) known impossible in their model, (b) open, (c) cheaply falsifiable.

claims: Ladder T1..T6 of intermediate ECDLP targets with exact models; T1 (Shoup/Maurer generic) and T2 (S T^2 = Omega~(eps N), Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan) known in their models; T4, T5, restricted-family T6 for prime fields with large embedding degree open. Status: unproved/literature survey; sources partly secondary.

Proof attempt (unreviewed, unformalized): Theorem A: f in F_q[X,Y] with f(kP)=k for 1<=k<=N<=r-1 has pole order >= (N-1)/2 and total degree >= (N-1)/6; rational version A' gives SLP length >= log2((N-1)/12). Likely duplicates Lange-Winterhof/Satoh (statements not seen).
Proof attempt, Lean candidate: Theorem B: g in F_p[X] with g(x(kP))=k^2 mod p for 1<=k<=(r-1)/2 has degree >= (r-5)/6 (elementary, no divisors).

Experimental (finite): 40 toy curves p<=109: minimal interpolation pole order = r and x-only minimal degree = (r-3)/2; 2519 identity checks for Theorem B with 0 failures. Supports only the tested domain.

O(n log n) target is below the double-and-add verification cost O(n^2 log n); algebraic F_q-SLPs computing k mod p need Omega(n) ops, Omega(n^2) bit ops under per-op charging Omega(log q) (model assumption).
